tagline: Regulated energy distribution company serving the New York metropolitan region with diversified revenue streams from electricity, natural gas, and steam delivery across multiple regulated jurisdictions
hero_kpi_rationale: Key performance indicator for regulated energy distribution companies, reflecting the diversified revenue base across electricity, natural gas, and steam in the service areas of New York and Westchester
company_description: Consolidated Edison, Inc., through its subsidiaries, engages in the regulated electric, gas, and steam delivery businesses in the United States. The company offers electric services to approximately 3.7 million customers in New York City and Westchester County; gas to approximately 1.1 million customers in Manhattan, the Bronx, parts of Queens, and Westchester County; and steam to approximately 1,490 customers in parts of Manhattan. It also supplies electricity to approximately 0.3 million customers in southeastern New York and northern New Jersey; and gas to approximately 0.1 million customers in southeastern New York. In addition, the company operates 552 circuit miles of transmission lines; 16 transmission substations; 63 distribution substations; 89,675 in-service line transformers; 3,764 pole miles of overhead distribution lines; and 2,417 miles of underground distribution lines, as well as 4,374 miles of mains and 379,939 service lines for natural gas distribution. Further, it invests in electric and gas transmission projects. The company primarily sells electricity to industrial, commercial, residential, and government customers. Consolidated Edison, Inc. was founded in 1823.

risks.title: Regulatory approval of investment plans
risks.summary: Planned investments of $6.5 to $8.5 billion per year and associated financing plans require approval from the New York regulator. Any denial or delay could block critical infrastructure projects.
risks.score_rationale: Risk positioned mid-report (p.8) with moderate language ('may differ materially'). Critical as 2026-2030 financing plans depend entirely on NYSPSC approval. Stable but structural trend. Regulation category = high weight for utility.

risks.title: Federal tax audit on tax calculations
risks.summary: The New York regulator is investigating an unintentional but potentially significant understatement of federal taxes reported by the Utilities for rate-setting purposes, particularly on asset retirement costs.
risks.score_rationale: Positioned at end of introduction (p.9) with explicit language ('material'). Ongoing NYSPSC audit on potentially material understatement of federal tax charges. New/increased (mentioned as 'continued'). Litigation/regulation category = high weight.

risks.title: Financing of $35 billion over 5 years
risks.summary: ED must raise approximately $35 billion over 2026-2030 through debt and equity issuances to finance its infrastructure investments. Any disruption in capital markets or rate increases could compromise this program.
risks.score_rationale: Positioned mid-report (p.8-9) with factual language but considerable volume ($35B+ 2026-2030). Depends on capital markets, equity and debt issuances. Stable trend but increasing scale ($8.5B in 2029-2030 vs $6.5B in 2026). Capital category = high weight.

risks.title: Cybersecurity of critical systems
risks.summary: ED operates electricity, gas, and steam distribution systems critical to New York. A cyberattack on this infrastructure could disrupt essential services and cause massive damage.
risks.score_rationale: Cybersecurity explicitly listed in Item 1C (p.47) of the table of contents, indicating a dedicated section. For a utility operating critical infrastructure (electricity, gas, steam), existential risk. Cybersecurity category = maximum weight. Stable trend but increasing sector threat.

risks.title: Energy demand and grid capacity
risks.summary: CECONY forecasts moderate electricity demand growth (0.7% annually) but O&R anticipates 4.1% annually. ED must invest heavily to avoid bottlenecks, particularly with increasing electrification.
risks.score_rationale: Positioned mid-introduction (p.8) with factual data on demand growth (0.7% electricity, 4.1% O&R). Stable trend but O&R shows accelerated growth. Risk that existing capacity may be insufficient. Industrial category = medium weight.

risks.title: Gas regulatory compliance (welds)
risks.summary: The New York regulator is examining CECONY gas pipeline welds. A $100 million reimbursement mechanism over 3 years has been incorporated into the rate plan, reflecting compliance risks.
risks.score_rationale: Positioned mid-introduction (p.9) with specific language on reimbursement mechanism. $100M risk over 2026-2028 for gas pipeline weld review. New/increased (related to NYSDPS audit). Regulation category = high weight.

risks.title: Mountain Valley Pipeline divestiture
risks.summary: ED Transmission is divesting its interest in Mountain Valley Pipeline (MVP), selling 40% and planning to sell the remainder in H1 2026 for $357.5 million. Reflects a strategic reorientation.
risks.score_rationale: Positioned mid-introduction (p.9) with neutral language ('completed', 'expects'). 40% sale completed, remainder in progress. $357.5M amount not material for ED. Down trend (strategic divestiture). Geopolitical/capital category = medium weight.
